claims: Artemis II is a ~10-day crewed mission.
Artemis II is scheduled for April 2026.
Artemis II will send four astronauts around the Moon and back.
Artemis II marks the first human journey beyond low-Earth orbit since 1972.
The Orion spacecraft will launch on the SLS rocket.
The Orion spacecraft will perform Earth-orbit system checks.
The Orion spacecraft will execute a translunar injection.
The Orion spacecraft will perform a crewed lunar flyby.
The Orion spacecraft will return to a Pacific Ocean splashdown.
On Day 1 of Artemis II, the SLS rocket places Orion into an initial high-Earth orbit.
During Days 1-2 of Artemis II, astronauts will separate from the ICPS upper stage, as reported by NASA and PBS News.
During Days 1-2 of Artemis II, astronauts will manually fly the spacecraft around the ICPS to test maneuvering capabilities, as reported by NASA and PBS News.
On Day 2 of Artemis II, Orion fires its engines to leave Earth's orbit and enter a free-return trajectory toward the Moon, according to WESH 2 News.
On Day 6 of Artemis II, the crew will swing around the far side of the Moon, notes the Planetary Society.
During the Artemis II lunar flyby on Day 6, the crew reaches distances up to 450,000 km from Earth, notes the Planetary Society.
On Day 10 of Artemis II, the spacecraft returns to Earth, hitting the atmosphere at roughly 25,000 mph (7 miles/second), as described by CBS News.
On Day 10 of Artemis II, the spacecraft endures temperatures near 5,000°F during re-entry, as described by CBS News.
Artemis II involves validating life-support, navigation, and propulsion systems with a human crew for the first time in deep space, according to ESA.
Artemis II involves testing manual controls for the spacecraft, per NASA.
A core objective of Artemis II is gathering data to prepare for Artemis III by ensuring safe landing of the first woman and next man on the Moon.
